frames.narration: A pull request swaps the support assistant to a cheaper model with a new prompt. The golden set has 200 graded questions; the current version passes 140 of them (70.0%).
Each question is answered by the new version, then graded against its rubric by the judge. Sampling makes answers vary from run to run, so the run is pinned to a model version and one fixed setting.

Before trusting the judge, 50 answers were also labelled by humans. It agreed on 44 (88%). It favoured the longer answer in 4 of its 6 disagreements, so answers are length-checked and shown in both orders.
The new version passes 147 of 200 (73.5%). On the same items it fixed 18 and broke 11, so the gap is +3.5 points with a 95% interval of -1.8 to +8.8. That includes zero: no proof it is better.
The rule was written first: block if the lower bound is below -2 points. -1.8 clears it, so the change may go to live traffic as safe to try, not as a proven improvement.
In week 1 the candidate also runs in shadow on live requests. Thumbs-down rate is 4.1% against 4.0% for the old version, and the cost per answer falls. The canary widens to 50%, then 100%.

In week 3 questions about a new product jump from 3% to 14% of traffic, and the refusal rate rises from 2% to 6%. The golden set has no such questions, so its score still looks fine: it is stale, not the model.

Humans label 100 sampled live failures and add them, so the golden set grows to 300. The new slice fails often, the flag flips back to the old version in minutes, and the next gate run uses the refreshed set.
